description: PCSWMM is a commercial modelling environment built around the US EPA Storm Water Management Model (SWMM5) and EPANET2. Its vendor, Computational Hydraulics International (CHI), describes it as a spatial decision support system for stormwater, wastewater, watershed and water distribution modelling, with a GIS engine that supports all SWMM5 and EPANET2 capabilities, tools for model design, optimisation, analysis, visualisation and project management, and no limit on model size. A Professional 2D tier adds integrated one- and two-dimensional modelling with directional, uniform, adaptive and irregular mesh generation, used for surface flooding from surcharged drainage networks. CHI also runs the open-access Journal of Water Management Modeling, the International Conference on Water Management Modeling and the OpenSWMM and OpenEPANET community sites. Coverage is generic: users build models of any catchment or network from their own data. Access: annual per-user subscriptions of 1,600 US dollars (Professional), 2,400 (Professional 2D) and 4,400 plus a 600 base cost (Enterprise, minimum three users), as listed on the pricing page read on 26 September 2026, with a free 30-day trial and educational grants. Caveats: proprietary and Windows desktop software; the simulation engines are the public SWMM5 and EPANET, so their assumptions carry over. Simulation uses: urban drainage network flow, pluvial flood hazard mapping, capacity planning and testing of climate adaptation such as green infrastructure. Related records: EPA SWMM (model-epa-swmm), EPANET (model-epanet) and the open-source Giswater platform (platform-giswater).
